capabilities.target: payments.issue_refund on any order up to order total

inputs.source: Requests from support staff via SSO authenticated channel

instructions.note: The prompt directs refund processing generally and says to use judgment on partial refunds without defining approval, amount, or policy bounds.
The prompt says not to ask for confirmation, substituting instruction for an external approval or policy check.

controls.name: SSO authenticated support staff request channel
controls.decay_rationale: Authentication identifies the requesting staff member at channel entry but does not constrain the refund sink or preserve attributable provenance through the processor action.

controls.name: Payments processor transaction log
controls.decay_rationale: The processor log records service account, amount, and order after the refund call, but it does not prevent improper refunds and does not attribute them to a staff requester.

controls.name: Tamper-evident attributable refund request and approval provenance
controls.decay_rationale: A system-bound record linking staff identity, reason, order, amount, and agent action would restore attribution independently of model behavior.

controls.name: Per-refund human approval gate with raw action review for irreversible refunds
controls.decay_rationale: A per-refund gate enforced outside the model would require human review of order, amount, and destination action before the irreversible processor call.

controls.name: Least-privilege delegated refund credentials bound to requester or policy scope
controls.decay_rationale: Requester-bound or narrower scoped credentials would prevent the agent from acting with organization-wide shared payment authority.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): trusted staff requests can trigger irreversible refunds through a shared service account with no approval gate

attack_path.note: Trusted support staff request reaches refund workflow.
Agent reads confidential order and payment details to prepare the refund.
Agent issues an irreversible refund using a shared service account.

forecast.watch_signal: Expansion of refund authority, wider processor credential grants, or workflow changes that increase unattended refund volume should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.
The prompt directs the agent to process refund requests, check the order, issue the refund, and not ask for confirmation.

recommendations.action: Add a per-refund human approval gate with raw action review for irreversible refunds, at least for partial refunds and higher amounts.
Replace the shared service account with requester-bound or narrowly scoped refund credentials so the agent cannot exercise broader refund authority than the requester is permitted to use.

findings.title: Missing attributable provenance for irreversible refunds leaves actions non-attributable to requesting staff

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended refund volume or retention changes that further reduce request traceability should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Create a tamper-evident action provenance record that binds each refund to the requesting staff identity, order, amount, justification, and agent execution record before submitting to the processor.
Retain refund request records long enough to support reconciliation and post-incident investigation, and correlate them with processor transaction identifiers.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts describe no self-configuration, prompt editing, tool definition changes, or writable memory surface for this agent design.
The design exposes no external send capability or other data egress path beyond the refund action itself, which is a spend sink rather than disclosure.
The workflow is short, bounded to order lookup and refund issuance, with no loops, spawning, or open-ended runtime described in the artifacts.
The artifacts state SSO authentication but do not describe message integrity, channel protections, or whether requests can be altered in transit.
The artifacts do not say whether support staff requests are encrypted in transit or logged with sensitive order details.
No request-rate, queue, or throttling details are provided for the inbound support staff request flow.
The artifacts do not describe transport integrity, replay protection, or processor-side request signing for the refund call.
The artifacts do not say whether refund calls or logs expose payment details outside the intended processor boundary.
No processor-side quotas, rate limits, or refund throughput controls are described for this outbound refund flow.
The artifacts do not state whether the processor log is tamper-evident or immutable, only that it records service account, amount, and order.
The artifacts do not describe who can read the processor log or whether it exposes confidential payment data beyond need-to-know.
Loss of availability of the processor log would hinder investigation but is not described as affecting refund execution in this design.
The design lacks this record entirely, so the artifacts cannot establish immutability or integrity protections for a provenance store.
Because no request provenance store exists, the artifacts provide no retention or access-control details for such records.
The absent provenance store is material to attribution, not to service availability, under the design facts provided.

rating.rationale: Present path risk from trusted staff requests to irreversible refunds is moderate because a trusted source reaches an S3 spend sink. The highest current risk is the property finding: irreversible refunds lack attributable provenance, since processor logs record only the shared service account and request chats are deleted after 7 days. No declared structural control restores attribution or constrains the shared refund authority, so residual remains high and forecast remains high under considered triggers. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run in this environment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, API schemas, processor configuration, retention policy documents, or runtime telemetry were provided, so transport integrity, exact authorization checks, and any hidden controls could not be verified.
No explicit approval workflow, refund policy thresholds, or processor-side rate limits were described; residual scoring therefore assumes the agent acts as declared without those controls.
